statement: If from an odd number an even number be subtracted, the remainder will be odd.
heath_proof: For from the odd number AB let the even number BC be subtracted; I say that the remainder CA is odd. Let the unit AD be subtracted; therefore DB is even. [VII. Def. 7] But BC is also even; therefore the remainder CD is even. [IX. 24] Therefore CA is odd. [VII. Def. 7]
ai_proof_text:
9.27
**Statement:** If from an odd number an even number be subtracted, the remainder will be odd.

**Step 1.** Let AB be an odd number, and from it let the even number BC be subtracted, the point C falling on AB so that the remainder is CA. I say that CA is odd.

**Step 2.** Since AB is odd, it differs by a unit from an even number [D7.7]. Let the unit AD be taken away from AB at the extremity A. Since CA, the remainder after subtracting BC from AB, is a number and so is not less than the unit, the point D falls on CA, so that the points A, D, C, B lie in order on AB. Then the remainder DB, being the odd number AB diminished by a unit, is even [D7.7].

**Step 3.** Now DB is even (Step 2), and BC is even by hypothesis, and BC is a part of DB. Therefore, the even number BC being subtracted from the even number DB, the remainder DC is even [9.24].

**Step 4.** But CA is made up of the even number CD together with the unit DA; that is, CA exceeds the even number CD by a unit. Therefore CA differs by a unit from an even number, and is therefore odd [D7.7].

**Step 5.** Therefore, if from an odd number an even number be subtracted, the remainder will be odd. Q.E.D.
